```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
set.seed(4131)
library(broom); library(knitr)
df <- read.csv("data/students.csv")      # knit_root_dir is the repository root
df$method <- factor(df$method)
```

# Objective
Investigate which factors influence exam performance among `r nrow(df)` students and whether teaching method matters.

# Data
`data/students.csv` (synthetic, produced by `data/generate_datasets.py`), `r ncol(df)` variables.

```{r desc}
kable(round(t(sapply(df[, c("study_hours", "attendance_pct", "sleep_hours", "prior_gpa", "exam_score")],
                     function(v) c(mean = mean(v), sd = sd(v), min = min(v), max = max(v)))), 2),
      caption = "Descriptive statistics")
```

# Methods
One-way ANOVA (teaching method), Pearson correlation (study hours) and multiple linear regression. Significance level 0.05.

# Results

```{r plots}
hist(df$exam_score, breaks = 20, col = "lightblue", border = "white", main = "Exam score distribution", xlab = "Score")
boxplot(exam_score ~ method, data = df, col = "lightblue", main = "Score by method")
plot(df$study_hours, df$exam_score, pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 1, .4), xlab = "Study hours", ylab = "Exam score")
abline(lm(exam_score ~ study_hours, df), col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

```{r models}
an <- summary(aov(exam_score ~ method, df))[[1]]
ct <- cor.test(df$study_hours, df$exam_score)
fit <- lm(exam_score ~ study_hours + attendance_pct + prior_gpa + method, df)
kable(tidy(fit), digits = 4, caption = "Regression coefficients")
```

* **ANOVA:** F = `r round(an[["F value"]][1], 2)`, p = `r signif(an[["Pr(>F)"]][1], 3)`
* **Correlation (study hours, score):** r = `r round(ct$estimate, 3)`, p = `r signif(ct$p.value, 3)`
* **Regression:** R-squared = `r round(summary(fit)$r.squared, 3)`

# Conclusions
1. Teaching method matters: mean scores differ significantly across methods.
2. Study hours is the strongest single predictor; each extra hour adds about `r round(coef(fit)[["study_hours"]], 2)` marks, controlling for other factors.
3. The model explains `r round(summary(fit)$r.squared * 100)`% of score variation.
4. The data are synthetic: the conclusions illustrate the method, not real students.
